'''Gediminas Juzeliūnas''' (born 14 July 1958) is a professor of [[theoretical physics]]<ref>[http://www.tfai.vu.lt/index.php?siteaction=personnel.view&id=181&menu=about Institute of Theoretical Physics and Astronomy]</ref> and heads the Quantum optics group<ref>[http://www.itpa.lt/quantumgroup/ Quantum optics group]</ref> at [[Vilnius University]] in [[Lithuania]]. He has authored and co-authored more than 50<ref>[https://arxiv.org/find/all/1/all:+juzeliunas_g/0/1/0/all/0/1 arXiv.org]</ref> articles on [[quantum optics|quantum]] and [[nonlinear optics]], as well as on theoretical [[condensed matter physics]].<ref name="MPC-object" />

Juzeliūnas is best known for putting forward realistic schemes in order to generate artificial [[spin–orbit interaction|spin-orbit coupling]] for ultracold atoms.<ref>[http://journals.aps.org/rmp/abstract/10.1103/RevModPhys.83.1523 Colloquium: Artificial gauge potentials for neutral atoms]</ref> These advances were essential in order to make an experimental connection between spintronics and cold atomic gases.<ref>[http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/2008/aug/01/cold-atoms-could-help-build-spintronics-transistor Cold atoms could help build 'spintronics' transistor]</ref><ref>[http://jqi.umd.edu/news/spin-control-modeling-transistor-future Spin Control: Modeling the Transistor of the Future]</ref> Furthermore, his landmark publications on slow light<ref>[http://www.nature.com/ncomms/2014/141124/ncomms6542/full/ncomms6542.html?WT.ec_id=NCOMMS-20141126 Experimental demonstration of spinor slow light]</ref> and artificial magnetic fields<ref>[http://physics.aps.org/articles/v2/25 Viewpoint: Artificial magnetism for ultracold atoms]</ref> have led to important insights in quantum optics and [[many-body physics]].<ref>[http://phys.org/news184402943.html Artificial magnetic fields for light could illuminate correlated quantum systems]</ref>

Asteroid [[289021 Juzeliunas]], discovered by astronomers [[Kazimieras Černis]] and [[Justas Zdanavičius]] in 2004, was named in his and his father's honor.<ref name="MPC-object" /> The official {{MoMP|289021|naming citation}} was published by the [[Minor Planet Center]] on 5 January 2015 ({{small|[[Minor Planet Circulars|M.P.C.]] 91793}}).<ref name="MPC-Circulars-Archive" />
